title: Dose makes the defense: hormone thresholds reprogram nematode immunity in rice
content: Root-knot nematodes such a Meloidogyne graminicola represent a major challenge for rice production, establishing long-lasting feeding sites that siphon host resources (Mantelin et al. 2017). While salicylic acid (SA) and jasmonic acid (JA) have well-established roles in nematode defense, abscisic acid (ABA) and ethylene (ET) have remained enigmatic, with reports of both resistance and susceptibility depending on context (Wubben et al. 2008; Nahar et al. 2011; Hu et al. 2017; Kyndt et al. 2017). Nevertheless, plant immunity is often described as a matter of hormones turning signaling pathways “on” or “off.”
